content: In France, the social security system ensures that prenatal and postnatal care in public hospitals is fully covered. Employed women are entitled to 16 weeks of maternity leave, with daily compensation ranging from €9.29 ($10.94) to €84.90 ($100), depending on their prior earnings. Financial concerns during pregnancy and around childbirth are similar to those experienced at other times: financially vulnerable families still face difficulties, but not to a greater extent, while wealthier families maintain their comfortable status. However, when it comes to support for new mothers, there is a clear gap. Paternity leave lasts just 11 days, which is insufficient for mothers to recover from childbirth. Consequently, new mothers must juggle the continuous responsibilities of their new role while healing and handle the challenge of finding childcare. State childcare programs, particularly in the Paris region, are inadequate. Childcare costs can vary significantly; daycare centers offer lower-income families a rate of about €1,000 ($1,177.59) per year, but there is only one spot available for every eight children, leading many families to rely on private services like childminders or home-based care. Any other questions?
